 environment varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(environment)>0),
 test_id uuid NOT NULL,
 secret_id varchar(64) NOT NULL CHECK(secret_id ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$'),
 vault_version varchar(256) CHECK(length(vault_version)>0),
 coordinate_step_id varchar(256) CHECK(length(coordinate_step_id)>0),
 coordinate_ordinal integer CHECK(coordinate_ordinal>=0),
 source_reference_id varchar(256) CHECK(length(source_reference_id)>0),
 outcome varchar(24) CHECK(outcome IN ('RESOLVED','NOT_AUTHORIZED','REVOKED',
  'UNAVAILABLE','VAULT_UNAVAILABLE','REVOKED_MID_RUN')),
 usage_outcome varchar(32),
 PRIMARY KEY(id,release_occurred_at),
 FOREIGN KEY(test_id,csi_id) REFERENCES ui_tests(id,csi_id),
 FOREIGN KEY(session_id,admission_id) REFERENCES studio_guided_actions(session_id,admission_id),
 CHECK((path='GUIDED' AND session_id IS NOT NULL AND execution_id IS NULL)
  OR (path='OBSERVED_REPLAY' AND execution_id IS NOT NULL AND session_id IS NULL)),
 CHECK(path<>'OBSERVED_REPLAY' OR (coordinate_step_id IS NULL AND coordinate_ordinal IS NULL AND source_reference_id IS NULL)),
 CHECK(path<>'GUIDED' OR coordinate_step_id IS NOT NULL),
 CHECK(occurred_at>=release_occurred_at),
 CONSTRAINT ck_secret_audit_row_shape CHECK((
  (row_kind='RELEASE' AND release_id=id AND release_seq IS NOT NULL AND outcome IS NOT NULL AND usage_outcome IS NULL
   AND (path<>'GUIDED' OR (admission_id IS NOT NULL AND coordinate_ordinal IS NOT NULL))
   AND ((decision_stage='DISPATCH' AND affected_release_id IS NULL
     AND outcome<>'REVOKED_MID_RUN' AND release_occurred_at=occurred_at)
    OR (decision_stage='LIVE_RECHECK' AND affected_release_id IS NOT NULL
     AND affected_release_id<>id AND outcome='REVOKED_MID_RUN')))
  OR (row_kind='USAGE' AND decision_stage IS NULL AND affected_release_id IS NULL
   AND usage_outcome IS NOT NULL
   AND ((release_id IS NOT NULL AND outcome IS NOT NULL AND release_seq IS NOT NULL
     AND (path<>'GUIDED' OR (admission_id IS NOT NULL AND coordinate_ordinal IS NOT NULL)))
    OR (release_id IS NULL AND outcome IS NULL AND vault_version IS NULL AND release_seq IS NULL
     AND release_occurred_at=occurred_at
     AND ((path='GUIDED' AND ((usage_outcome='NOT_USED' AND admission_id IS NULL
       AND coordinate_ordinal IS NULL AND source_reference_id IS NOT NULL)
      OR (usage_outcome IN ('UNKNOWN_OUTCOME','ACK_LOST') AND admission_id IS NOT NULL AND coordinate_ordinal IS NOT NULL)))
      OR (path='OBSERVED_REPLAY' AND usage_outcome IN ('NOT_USED','UNKNOWN_OUTCOME') AND admission_id IS NULL)))))
 ) IS TRUE),
 CHECK(row_kind<>'USAGE' OR
  (path='OBSERVED_REPLAY' AND usage_outcome IN ('USED','NOT_USED','REFUSED','UNKNOWN_OUTCOME')) OR
  (path='GUIDED' AND usage_outcome IN ('USED','NOT_USED','REFUSED','OK','ASSERTION_FAILED',
   'TARGET_CHANGED','POLICY_DENIED','TIMEOUT','ACK_LOST','UNKNOWN_OUTCOME','CANCELLED'))),
 CHECK(row_kind<>'RELEASE' OR outcome<>'RESOLVED' OR vault_version IS NOT NULL)
) PARTITION BY RANGE(release_occurred_at);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_secret_usage_release ON studio_secret_use_audit(release_id,release_occurred_at)
 WHERE row_kind='USAGE' AND release_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_secret_live_recheck ON studio_secret_use_audit(affected_release_id,release_occurred_at)
 WHERE decision_stage='LIVE_RECHECK';
CREATE INDEX ix_secret_audit_session ON studio_secret_use_audit(session_id,secret_id,release_occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_secret_audit_execution ON studio_secret_use_audit(execution_id,secret_id,release_occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_secret_audit_scope ON studio_secret_use_audit(csi_id,test_id,occurred_at);

-- Safe, positively constructed read/no-send evidence; neither family is retry authority.
CREATE TABLE studio_observed_secret_read_entries (
 id uuid NOT NULL, occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(occurred_at)),
 execution_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studio_dispatch_ledger(execution_id),
 execution_accepted_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(execution_accepted_at)),
 attempt_id uuid NOT NULL, revision_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ui_test_revisions(id),
 revision_digest char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(revision_digest ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 binding_digest char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(binding_digest ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 scope_hash char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(scope_hash ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 principal_id varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(principal_id)>0),
 csi_id varchar(20) NOT NULL, environment varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(environment)>0),
 test_id uuid NOT NULL, lease_owner varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(lease_owner)>0),
 secret_id varchar(64) NOT NULL CHECK(secret_id ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$'),
 PRIMARY KEY(id,occurred_at), FOREIGN KEY(test_id,csi_id) REFERENCES ui_tests(id,csi_id)
) PARTITION BY RANGE(occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_observed_read_entry_attempt ON studio_observed_secret_read_entries(execution_id,attempt_id,secret_id);
CREATE TABLE studio_observed_no_send_decisions (
 id uuid NOT NULL, occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(occurred_at)),
 execution_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studio_dispatch_ledger(execution_id),
 execution_accepted_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(execution_accepted_at)),
 attempt_id uuid NOT NULL, revision_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ui_test_revisions(id),
 revision_digest char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(revision_digest ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 binding_digest char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(binding_digest ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 scope_hash char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(scope_hash ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 principal_id varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(principal_id)>0),
 csi_id varchar(20) NOT NULL, environment varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(environment)>0),
 test_id uuid NOT NULL, lease_owner varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(lease_owner)>0),
 not_entered_ids jsonb NOT NULL, disposition varchar(8) NOT NULL CHECK(disposition IN ('CLOSED','REQUEUED')),
 PRIMARY KEY(id,occurred_at), FOREIGN KEY(test_id,csi_id) REFERENCES ui_tests(id,csi_id),
 CHECK(jsonb_typeof(not_entered_ids)='array' AND jsonb_array_length(not_entered_ids)<=64)
) PARTITION BY RANGE(occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_observed_no_send_attempt ON studio_observed_no_send_decisions(execution_id,attempt_id);

-- Terminal winners have separate CLOSED-only authority; no live lease is borrowed.
CREATE TABLE studio_observed_terminal_secret_settlements (
 id uuid NOT NULL, occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(occurred_at)),
 execution_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studio_dispatch_ledger(execution_id),
 execution_accepted_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(execution_accepted_at)),
 attempt_id uuid NOT NULL, revision_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ui_test_revisions(id),
 revision_digest char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(revision_digest ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 binding_digest char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(binding_digest ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 scope_hash char(64) NOT NULL CHECK(scope_hash ~ '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'),
 principal_id varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(principal_id)>0), csi_id varchar(20) NOT NULL,
 environment varchar(256) NOT NULL CHECK(length(environment)>0), test_id uuid NOT NULL,
 disposition varchar(6) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CLOSED' CHECK(disposition='CLOSED'),
 before_state varchar(16) NOT NULL CHECK(before_state IN ('QUEUED','CLAIMED')),
 before_updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL, before_snapshot_revision bigint NOT NULL,
 before_ended_at timestamptz, terminal_error_code varchar(64) NOT NULL CHECK(terminal_error_code ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$'),
 terminal_ended_at timestamptz NOT NULL CHECK(isfinite(terminal_ended_at)),
 no_read_ids jsonb NOT NULL, possible_read_ids jsonb NOT NULL,
 PRIMARY KEY(id,occurred_at), FOREIGN KEY(test_id,csi_id) REFERENCES ui_tests(id,csi_id)
) PARTITION BY RANGE(occurred_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_observed_terminal_attempt ON studio_observed_terminal_secret_settlements(execution_id,attempt_id);

-- VOLATILE is deliberate: after a waited owner lock, SPI reads use the fresh current snapshot.
CREATE FUNCTION studio_observed_terminal_classification(execution_key uuid,attempt_key uuid) RETURNS jsonb
 LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE AS $$
DECLARE result jsonb; declarations jsonb; owner_row studio_dispatch_ledger; history_row ui_test_executions;
BEGIN
 SELECT * INTO STRICT owner_row FROM studio_dispatch_ledger WHERE execution_id=execution_key;
 SELECT * INTO STRICT history_row FROM ui_test_executions WHERE id=execution_key AND started_at=owner_row.execution_accepted_at;
 IF EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM studio_observed_secret_read_entries entry WHERE entry.execution_id=execution_key
  AND entry.attempt_id=attempt_key AND ROW(entry.execution_accepted_at,entry.revision_id,entry.revision_digest::text,
   entry.binding_digest::text,entry.scope_hash::text,entry.principal_id,entry.csi_id,entry.environment,entry.test_id)
   IS DISTINCT FROM ROW(owner_row.execution_accepted_at,history_row.revision_id,
    history_row.observed_revision_binding->>'revisionDigest',studio_publication_hash(history_row.observed_revision_binding),
    history_row.observed_revision_binding->>'scopeHash',owner_row.principal,owner_row.csi_id,history_row.environment,owner_row.test_id)) THEN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'terminal secret read-entry scope mismatch'; END IF;
 SELECT r."references"->'secrets' INTO STRICT declarations FROM studio_dispatch_ledger l
  JOIN ui_test_executions e ON e.id=l.execution_id AND e.started_at=l.execution_accepted_at
  JOIN ui_test_revisions r ON r.id=e.revision_id AND r.test_id=l.test_id AND r.csi_id=l.csi_id
  WHERE l.execution_id=execution_key AND e.observed_revision_binding->>'attemptId'=attempt_key::text;
 IF jsonb_typeof(declarations) IS DISTINCT FROM 'array' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'terminal secret declaration unavailable'; END IF;
 IF jsonb_array_length(declarations)>64 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements(declarations) name
  WHERE jsonb_typeof(name)<>'string' OR name#>>'{}' !~ '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$')
  OR (SELECT count(*) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text(declarations))<>
     (SELECT count(DISTINCT name) FROM jsonb_array_elements_text(declarations) name) THEN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'terminal secret declaration invalid'; END IF;
 SELECT jsonb_build_object('noReadIds',COALESCE(jsonb_agg(name ORDER BY name) FILTER(WHERE NOT entered),'[]'::jsonb),
  'possibleReadIds',COALESCE(jsonb_agg(name ORDER BY name) FILTER(WHERE entered),'[]'::jsonb)) INTO result
 FROM (SELECT name,EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM studio_observed_secret_read_entries entry
   WHERE entry.execution_id=execution_key AND entry.attempt_id=attempt_key AND entry.secret_id=name) AS entered
  FROM jsonb_array_elements_text(declarations) name
  WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM studio_secret_use_audit fact WHERE fact.execution_id=execution_key
    AND fact.attempt_id=attempt_key::text AND fact.secret_id=name
    AND (fact.decision_stage='DISPATCH' OR fact.row_kind='USAGE'))) remaining;
 RETURN result;
END $$;

CREATE FUNCTION studio_observed_terminal_insert_guard() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE l studio_dispatch_ledger; e ui_test_executions; expected jsonb;
BEGIN
 SELECT * INTO STRICT l FROM studio_dispatch_ledger WHERE execution_id=NEW.execution_id FOR UPDATE;
 SELECT * INTO STRICT e FROM ui_test_executions WHERE id=l.execution_id AND started_at=l.execution_accepted_at FOR UPDATE;
 PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('studio-secret-audit-owner:OBSERVED_REPLAY:'||NEW.execution_id::text,0));
 PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('studio-secret-terminal-id:'||NEW.id::text,0));
 IF (l.state IN ('QUEUED','CLAIMED') AND l.attempt_id IS NULL AND l.admission_id IS NULL
  AND e.status='PENDING' AND e.observed_admission_receipt IS NULL AND e.observed_revision_binding IS NOT NULL
  AND e.observed_revision_binding->>'attemptId'=NEW.attempt_id::text
  AND ROW(l.execution_accepted_at,e.revision_id,e.observed_revision_binding->>'revisionDigest',
   studio_publication_hash(e.observed_revision_binding),e.observed_revision_binding->>'scopeHash',
   l.principal,l.csi_id,e.environment,l.test_id)
   IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ROW(NEW.execution_accepted_at,NEW.revision_id,NEW.revision_digest::text,
    NEW.binding_digest::text,NEW.scope_hash::text,NEW.principal_id,NEW.csi_id,NEW.environment,NEW.test_id)) IS NOT TRUE THEN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'terminal secret settlement requires authentic pre-transition owner';
 END IF;
 IF (NEW.before_state IS NOT NULL AND NEW.before_state IS DISTINCT FROM l.state)
  OR (NEW.before_updated_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.before_updated_at IS DISTINCT FROM l.updated_at)
  OR (NEW.before_snapshot_revision IS NOT NULL AND NEW.before_snapshot_revision IS DISTINCT FROM e.snapshot_revision)
  OR (NEW.before_ended_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.before_ended_at IS DISTINCT FROM e.ended_at) THEN
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'terminal secret settlement before-image mismatch'; END IF;
 NEW.before_state:=l.state;NEW.before_updated_at:=l.updated_at;NEW.before_snapshot_revision:=e.snapshot_revision;
 NEW.before_ended_at:=e.ended_at;
 IF e.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN NEW.terminal_ended_at:=e.ended_at; END IF;

-- V15__studio_dispatch_ledger_state_machine.sql
-- Story 10.7 (10.7a) — the two CHECK constraints V13 deferred to this story.
-- Source: Architecture "Checks UI Studio" v2.1 §5.1 (acceptance, dispatch, admission),
--         §5.4 (recovery), §8.1 (dispatch ledger). Story 10.7 AC-2.
--
-- Forward-only. Applies after V14. Adding a CHECK to a merged table cannot be done by editing
-- V13, which is why this is a new migration rather than an amendment; it is the ONE migration
-- this story adds, and every column AC-2 through AC-31 needs already exists on V13 or V14.
--
-- The version number was a merge-time fact, not a drafting-time one: V12, V13 and V14 are merged
-- and other Epic-10 branches are in flight, so the story deliberately left it unassigned and it
-- is assigned here as the next free version.

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. The dispatch state vocabulary (AC-2)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The enumerated set is exactly V13's provisional list, unchanged and deliberately so. V13
-- already ships three partial indexes written against this vocabulary and against a SINGLE
-- absorbing terminal state:
--
--     idx_studio_dispatch_ledger_queued          WHERE state IN ('QUEUED','CLAIMED','DISPATCHING')
--     idx_studio_dispatch_ledger_start_deadline  WHERE state <> 'DONE' AND start_deadline_at IS NOT NULL
--     idx_studio_dispatch_ledger_run_deadline    WHERE state <> 'DONE' AND run_deadline_at IS NOT NULL
--
-- Widening or renaming the set would silently strand the indexes the reapers query through, so
-- the vocabulary is inherited rather than designed a second time.
--
-- state is a DISPATCH state and never an outcome: DONE covers success, error, disablement and
-- reaped work alike, and the outcome plus error_code live on the execution history row (§8.2)
-- and are not duplicated here.
--
-- Existing rows: the only values any writer has ever produced are 'QUEUED' (the column default
-- and the entity's constructor) and 'DONE' (V14's partition-locator backfill). Both are in the
-- set, so this applies to a database holding history as well as to an empty one — which
-- LedgerStateMachineMigrationIT proves by seeding rows at V14 and migrating afterwards, the
-- blind spot that hid V14's own browser-CHECK ordering defect.
ALTER TABLE studio_dispatch_ledger
    ADD CONSTRAINT ck_studio_dispatch_ledger_state
    CHECK (state IN ('QUEUED', 'CLAIMED', 'DISPATCHING', 'ADMITTED', 'RUNNING', 'FINALIZING', 'DONE'));

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. Admission identity is all-or-nothing (AC-2)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The admission CAS guards on (execution_id, attempt_id, admission_id, runner_instance_id), and
-- every runner report is applied by a statement carrying all four. A half-written identity —
-- an admission_id with no attempt_id or no runner_instance_id — is therefore a CAS guard with a
-- hole in it: the predicate would be satisfiable by a row nobody owns.
--
-- The converse is deliberately NOT constrained: an attempt_id without an admission_id is the
-- normal DISPATCHING state, which is precisely the window the CAS exists to close.
ALTER TABLE studio_dispatch_ledger
    ADD CONSTRAINT ck_studio_dispatch_ledger_admission_identity
    CHECK (admission_id IS NULL
           OR (attempt_id IS NOT NULL AND runner_instance_id IS NOT NULL));

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. Where the snapshot revision lives (AC-23)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- ui_test_executions.snapshot_revision is the authoritative monotonic revision: it is the SSE
-- event id and the `revision` of the public snapshot, and it is incremented by the same UPDATE
-- that makes each visible change. studio_dispatch_ledger.snapshot_revision is left at its V13
-- default and is not written by story 10.7: two allocators for one number is how they diverge.
COMMENT ON COLUMN studio_dispatch_ledger.snapshot_revision IS
    'Unused as of story 10.7: ui_test_executions.snapshot_revision is the single allocator of the '
    'public snapshot revision and the SSE event id (§5.5, AC-23).';

COMMENT ON COLUMN studio_dispatch_ledger.state IS
    'Dispatch state, never an outcome. QUEUED|CLAIMED|DISPATCHING|ADMITTED|RUNNING|FINALIZING|DONE; '
    'DONE is the single absorbing terminal state and covers success, error, disablement and reaped '
    'work alike (§8.1, story 10.7 AC-2/AC-3).';
-- V14__studio_execution_history_v2.sql
-- Story 10.1 — execution history carries immutable provenance, evidence state and real timings.
-- Source: Architecture "Checks UI Studio" v2.1 §5.3 (durable progress/results), §6.1 (evidence
--         state), §8.1 (execution history), §8.2 (execution migrations and states),
--         §8.3 (canonical browser value).
--
-- Forward-only. Applies after V12 (ui_test_revisions) and V13 (dispatch ledger).
--
-- ui_test_executions is range-partitioned by started_at with primary key (id, started_at)
-- since V7. started_at stays the immutable acceptance/partition timestamp and is never
-- rewritten; the public contract exposes it as acceptedAt. Browser start goes to the new
-- nullable browser_started_at, exposed as startedAt. ALTER TABLE on the partitioned parent
-- recurses into every partition, including the DEFAULT one.

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. Execution history columns (§8.1, §8.2, §6.1)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions
    -- Browser start; null until an authenticated runner start report is committed (§8.2).
    ADD COLUMN browser_started_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    -- Timeouts are ERROR with a code, never a distinct status (§8.2).
    ADD COLUMN error_code            VARCHAR(40),
    -- Immutable provenance. A partitioned table may reference a regular table, so this
    -- single-column FK into the unpartitioned ui_test_revisions is valid (V12).
    ADD COLUMN revision_id           UUID REFERENCES ui_test_revisions(id),
    -- The execution's own CSI. Historical access uses this, never a mutable parent lookup (§9.1).
    ADD COLUMN csi_id                VARCHAR(20),
    ADD COLUMN principal             VARCHAR(255),
    ADD COLUMN environment           VARCHAR(50),
    -- Nonsecret configuration snapshot taken at acceptance time.
    ADD COLUMN configuration_snapshot JSONB,
    -- One entry per original step: {stepIndex, originalText, status, offsetMs, durationMs, message}.
    ADD COLUMN step_results          JSONB,
    ADD COLUMN logs_truncated        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    -- Evidence: object key only; the browser is given the protected API path (§6.2, §6.3).
    ADD COLUMN video_key             TEXT,
    ADD COLUMN video_status          VARCHAR(20),
    ADD COLUMN video_error           TEXT,
    ADD COLUMN video_expires_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    ADD COLUMN video_partial         BOOLEAN,
    -- Actual runtime versions observed for this run (§4.6). Null for legacy history.
    ADD COLUMN runtime_versions      JSONB,
    -- Monotonic API snapshot revision; also the SSE event id (§5.5).
    ADD COLUMN snapshot_revision     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

-- Evidence state is independent of the check outcome (§6.1): an upload failure never overwrites
-- a known assertion outcome.
ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions ADD CONSTRAINT ck_ui_test_executions_video_status
    CHECK (video_status IS NULL
           OR video_status IN ('PROCESSING', 'AVAILABLE', 'FAILED', 'UNAVAILABLE', 'EXPIRED'));

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. Structured bounded log storage (§5.3, §8.1)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The legacy `logs TEXT` column becomes the structured buffer the snapshot contract exposes.
-- Legacy free text is preserved verbatim as a single INFO entry rather than discarded; nothing
-- is invented beyond the timestamp already recorded on the row.
ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions
    ALTER COLUMN logs TYPE JSONB
    USING CASE
        WHEN logs IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
                 'at', to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'),
                 'level', 'INFO',
                 'message', logs,
                 'stepIndex', NULL))
    END;

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. Status vocabulary and nullable end/duration (§8.2)
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Legacy outcome adapters applied in place: COMPLETED is PASSED; TIMEOUT is ERROR with a code.
-- The V1/V7 CHECK never allowed these values, so this normally updates zero rows; it exists so
-- that history restored from an older dump converges on the canonical vocabulary.
UPDATE ui_test_executions SET status = 'PASSED' WHERE status = 'COMPLETED';
UPDATE ui_test_executions
   SET status = 'ERROR', error_code = COALESCE(error_code, 'TIMEOUT')
 WHERE status = 'TIMEOUT';

-- Drop whatever the V1/V7 inline CHECK on status was named, then install the widened one.
-- Dropping on the partitioned parent propagates to every partition.
DO $$
DECLARE
    r RECORD;
BEGIN
    FOR r IN
        SELECT con.conname
          FROM pg_constraint con
          JOIN pg_attribute att
            ON att.attrelid = con.conrelid
           AND att.attnum = ANY(con.conkey)
         WHERE con.conrelid = 'ui_test_executions'::regclass
           AND con.contype = 'c'
           AND att.attname = 'status'
    LOOP
        EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions DROP CONSTRAINT %I', r.conname);
    END LOOP;
END
$$;

-- PENDING is accepted-but-not-browser-started; RUNNING requires a committed start report (§8.2).
-- This is also what makes the existing POST /tests/{id}/execute placeholder, which writes
-- PENDING, stop violating the constraint it was written against.
ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions ADD CONSTRAINT ck_ui_test_executions_status
    CHECK (status IN ('PENDING', 'RUNNING', 'PASSED', 'FAILED', 'ERROR'));

-- A run that has not finished has no end and no duration. durationMs measures browser execution
-- only; queue time is a separate budget (§8.2).
ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions ALTER COLUMN ended_at    DROP NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE ui_test_executions ALTER COLUMN duration_ms DROP NOT NULL;

-- 4. CSI backfill and quarantine of ambiguous history (§8.2)

Authority: fresh corrected Pax GO `t2-t3-po-bootstrap-closure-revalidation.json`, applied exact text in `bootstrap-closure-application/receipt.json`; root explicit D/B release follows source-bound root143/D41 baseline. This is development design, no QA/lifecycle verdict.

Planned error/time are proposals only, independently compared with actual winning history at commit; any existing history endedAt is captured for the close COALESCE rule. No lease is supplied or borrowed; a lost/expired claim can be closed by the actual terminal winner under the existing state matrix. The API is `boolean recordObservedTerminalSettlement(UUID executionId, String plannedErrorCode, Instant plannedEndedAt)` in the actual caller transaction before its terminal transition. Non-observed/ineligible/already-terminal owners append nothing; raw attempted insertion against a wrong before-image refuses. Empty remaining declaration inventory needs no new receipt.

The insertion guard independently locks the actual owner and history, requires QUEUED/CLAIMED, no dispatch attempt/admission/observed receipt and PENDING history, and captures/compares the actual before-image. After any waited owner lock it runs a separate fresh VOLATILE SQL statement for current declared IDs and committed scoped read entries; Java classification is also post-lock. Existing actual decisions or summaries take precedence and are excluded. Caller state/error labels/booleans cannot establish before-image or choose omitted/invented IDs. Exact accepted no-read IDs under B's universally enforced committed write-before-value-read protocol settle NOT_USED; exact possible entries with no committed decision settle audit-only UNKNOWN_OUTCOME. No version/resolution/use/refusal is inferred from a marker, and physical read counters remain separate joined evidence.

Pending terminal receipt fences new read-entry, RELEASE and dispatch/admission/requeue transitions. The only subsequent execution-authority transition is actual DONE, with terminal ERROR history. B generic close, immediate cancel, pending reaper and kill-switch preserve their existing predicates; request-only cancel/losers do not invoke a successful receipt or throw to roll back if CAS loses. Every receipt/complete new summary and owner/history update commits or rolls back in the same physical REQUIRED transaction.

Deferred guards on current/future plain leaves require owner, history, receipt and new summary row versions to belong to the current top-level PostgreSQL transaction, with exact locator/binding/attempt and complete classification. Savepoint/subtransaction writes for these transitions are deliberately prohibited by this top-XID invariant and tested as refusals. No transaction ID is persisted as long-term identity. Immediate cancellation need not populate generic close terminal_error fields; its actual ERROR/CANCELLED history/time, DONE owner/cancel marker and advancing snapshot must match the proposal. Generic populated owner terminal fields must match as well. Both actual owner/history row versions must be this transaction.

Immutable parent/leaf UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE and initial/future partition installation are mandatory. Existing live-owned completed-resolution no-send CLOSED/REQUEUED/outage authority remains separate and unchanged. No new wire field/enum or additional provider read/send is introduced.

Actual B provider/control crash/read/send/cancel/reaper/kill-switch and Core joins remain mandatory; data fixtures prove SQL/transaction/race metadata only. The retained pre-amendment zero-summary oracle will map explicitly to one authentic UNKNOWN after an entered/no-decision terminal winner; historical result remains preserved.

The retained read marker is conservative possible-read evidence, not authority for another read. B's fresh committed-entry verifier requires creator lease_owner to match the actual current owned claim before calling the provider. An abandoned marker under another owner therefore cannot authorize an extra value call on the same accepted attempt. Terminal classification still includes that scoped marker as UNKNOWN rather than false NOT_USED; a genuine outage/definite-refusal fresh attempt carries its own marker. No database receipt proves a physical read count.

# Checks UI Studio — Architecture

**Version:** 2.1 · **Date:** 2026-09-10 · **Status:** Design baseline; staging validation outstanding

**Compiler amendment (2026-09-16):** [Studio inference contract v1](studio-inference-contract-v1.md) supersedes affected §§4/8 compiler decisions for the remediation stories: explicit unsupported outcomes, strict verdicts, atomic request/candidate identity, bounded inference, and versioned full/incremental authoring. Its [versioned OpenAPI](../specs/studio/inference.openapi.yaml) is declared, not yet deployed. Existing positional runner artifacts/routes remain unchanged.

This document defines component ownership and technical contracts. [PRD §5.2](../../PRD.md#52-ui-testing-feature-checks-studio) and the [BRD](../brd/checks-ui-studio.brd.md) define product scope and GA criteria; [Epic 10](../epics/EPIC-10-EXECUTION.yaml) and its stories contain implementation order and acceptance tests. The [review](studio-execution-review.md) and [SSE assessment](studio-sse-viability.md) retain decision rationale.

## 1. Overview

A support engineer writes an English checklist, reviews the proposed actions and Playwright source, confirms a revision, and runs it. Studio shows live step/log progress and private video evidence. Confirmed instructions remain immutable; application state and browser timing can still change outcomes.

The editor, polling UI, video player and backend CRUD exist. Compilation, real execution, SSE and evidence storage remain to be built. Identity and vault code still contain temporary behavior; production-capable integrations are prerequisites for the credentialed pilot.

## 2. Scope

| Capability | V1 | Later / excluded |
|---|---|---|
| Authoring | CSI-scoped English steps, variables/secret references, confirmed TypeScript artifact | No runtime AI or hand-written English translator; Python export retired |
| Execution | On demand, Chromium, one page, initially one run per pod and 1–2 runner replicas | Scheduling, larger pools, other browsers, iframe/popup/multi-page workflows |
| Progress | SSE current-state snapshots with GET recovery/fallback | Lossless event replay, WebSockets and live video |
| Evidence | Native webm, private storage/download, attempted-step seek, 30-day expiry | Screenshots, transcoding and public video URLs |
| Platform integration | Studio history and last-run summaries by CSI | Unified UI_TEST catalog/application-component/dashboard/report projections |

Unsupported workflows must be explained before confirmation where detectable and fail explicitly otherwise. Pilot applications must support the approved single-page login flow; enterprise MFA is not assumed to work.

**Create:** MFE → backend → LLM proposal → runner validation → persisted candidate → user confirmation. The backend owns the approval and revision; no browser starts during compilation.

**Execute:** backend commits accepted work → worker claims it and resolves authorized references → runner obtains admission, runs Chromium and uploads evidence → backend persists reports and serves SSE/video. The worker reconciles lost results from storage. The MFE never talks directly to the runner.

The backend API and worker share the Java codebase but run under separate profiles with dedicated Studio limits. The new `studio-runner/` has its own image/Deployment and is the only component launching Chromium. The compiler is a logical capability split between API orchestration and runner validation, not another service. PostgreSQL is authoritative across API replicas. The Checks squad owns operations, supported by Platform/SRE for cluster, ingress and storage.

## 4. Studio Step Compiler

### 4.1 Principles

Compile on source changes or explicit recompile, never on execute. Draft persistence is independent of gateway availability; source/configuration changes follow §4.2.

The R2D2 LLM gateway proposes source. Static validation enforces permitted operations; it cannot prove the locator matches the application or the assertion captures the user's intent. The application DOM is not an input in V1. Representative internal workflows and observed runs/video are required to measure translation quality.

R2D2 is a proxy in front of Vertex-hosted models, so the backend integrates through the **Google Vertex AI SDK** rather than a bespoke HTTP client: use the Vertex generative-model client with its endpoint/base URL, project and location pointed at R2D2, and the service credentials issued for the Studio compile workload. Endpoint, project, location and credentials are deployment configuration (§8.5); none are hardcoded. Keeping the SDK contract means request/response shapes, structured output and timeout handling stay standard, but the proxy remains the authority on which models, parameters and quotas are actually reachable. Verify the supported SDK version, model identifiers and structured-output behavior against R2D2 in staging (§10) before relying on them, and disable SDK-level automatic retries that could exceed the bounded compile attempts in §4.3.

### 4.2 Revision and confirmation lifecycle

- `sourceRevision` advances on step edits; `configurationRevision` advances on execution-affecting configuration changes. Optimistic concurrency rejects stale saves with 409.
- Compilation states: `STALE | COMPILING | AWAITING_CONFIRMATION | READY | NEEDS_REVISION`.
- Persist a compile request identity with source revision before asynchronous work. Publish its result only if both still match; discard out-of-order results, including an older compile for the same text.
- Successful validation creates an immutable candidate revision containing source, source hash, artifact hash, nonsecret configuration, token references, and provenance. It becomes `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`; invalid candidates remain unrunnable with per-step diagnostics.
- Confirm with `{ revisionId, artifactHash, sourceRevision, configurationRevision }`. A conditional transaction verifies that this is still the current valid candidate and records `confirmedBy` and `confirmedAt` before setting `READY`. A stale tab gets 409.
- Configuration-only changes create a new candidate using compatible validated source and require reconfirmation. Changes include environment, variable values/references, viewport, timeout, browser, and target policy selection. Name/description changes do not invalidate confirmation.
- Vault value rotation does not require embedding a value or recompile; execution records a nonsecret vault version identifier when available. Artifacts pin references, not secret contents.

### 4.3 Prompt inputs and limits

Inputs: the ordered source steps fenced as data, the versioned Playwright syntax reference, and the output/allowed-language contract. Secret and variable references remain opaque (`<secret ID>`, `<var NAME>`). Never supply resolved values or dump request bodies into gateway audit logs.

Enforce input/output byte and step limits, gateway timeouts, bounded compile concurrency, and a maximum of two repair attempts. Inline credentials are prohibited in authoring; guide users to vault references and reject known credential patterns before gateway submission. Pattern checks cannot detect every pasted secret and must not be described as a proof that arbitrary text is secret-free.

Pin model, prompt, language-policy, syntax-reference, Playwright package/browser image and trusted-executor versions; CI validates reference examples against that runtime. Temperature zero/structured output reduce variance but do not guarantee reproducibility. A future cache must key all ordered source/context/version inputs and isolate CSIs.

### 4.4 Source artifact

The harness invokes trusted Playwright functions from validated nodes; it never uses `eval`, `Function`, async IIFEs, or Node VM as a security boundary. Runner revalidation uses the same policy and rejects incompatible artifacts before browser launch. Browser work runs in a killable child process with a parent-enforced deadline; control/validation endpoints have separate bounded resources.

**Text-entry role equivalence (executor 2.1.0, VAL-031).** For `fill` and `press`, a terminal `getByRole` with role `textbox`, `searchbox` or `combobox` (options limited to `name`/`exact`/`disabled`) means "the text-entry control with that accessible name". The authored role is always tried first and wins whenever it matches. Only after it has matched nothing for `min(2 s, timeout/4)` does the runner try the other two roles with the same options, and it acts only when exactly one element matches. Several matches are refused, and the runner never picks the first one. Every use is logged to the operator. This is a versioned, documented executor semantic, not a silent reinterpretation: an artifact that resolves on its authored role behaves exactly as under 2.0.0, with one exception: visible-only resolution, described next. See `studio-runner/README.md`.

**Visible-only resolution of actions (executor 2.1.0, VAL-040).** For the action operations (`click`, `fill`, `press`, `check`, `uncheck`, `hover`, `selectOption`), the runner narrows the locator to its visible matches (`filter({ visible: true })`) before applying strict mode. Hidden elements can't be acted on, so they no longer make a step ambiguous. Two or more visible matches still fail with the strict-mode message, where N is the visible count. Exactly one is acted on. If none is visible by the deadline, the step fails as "not visible", or as "no element matched" when nothing matched at all. The runner never uses `.first()`. Assertions resolve the unfiltered locator and are unchanged. `force: true` opts out. Under text-entry equivalence, the same filter applies to the authored role and to the alternatives. Each time the filter changes the outcome, the runner logs one operator line, `visible-only-resolution: step=<i> total=<n>`.

This restriction limits executable capabilities, not semantic mistakes or all prompt injection. Valid browser actions can still be harmful; destination and secret-use policy in §9 remain mandatory. [Node VM documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/vm.html) explicitly excludes VM contexts as a security mechanism.

### 4.6 Readiness and runtime compatibility

Execute only when the current confirmed revision matches the draft's source/configuration revisions and artifact hash, all steps validated, and current target/runtime policy permits it. Otherwise return `409 COMPILE_REQUIRED` or `409 RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE` as applicable. Server enforcement is authoritative.

Model changes never rewrite existing revisions. Runtime upgrades revalidate compatibility and run a fixture corpus before release; record actual runtime versions on executions. A revoked policy may block an old revision. Preserve it for history, and explain why it is blocked. Do not silently reinterpret it or keep a vulnerable runtime indefinitely to preserve replay.

### 4.7 User experience and failure handling

Show the original step, a readable action/target/assertion summary derived from validated operations, and expandable executable source. Unsupported/ambiguous instructions receive actionable diagnostics; observed execution/video verifies the proposed interpretation.

Gateway outage saves the draft and leaves compilation `STALE` with an error. Exhausted repair yields `NEEDS_REVISION`. Recovery of an abandoned compile request marks it retryable without replacing the confirmed history. All gateway calls carry audit metadata (test, CSI, user, model/prompt versions, latency, outcome), never resolved values.

## 5. Execution & runner

### 5.1 Acceptance and dispatch

1. `POST /tests/{id}/execute` checks identity, CSI execute permission, readiness, input limits, execution-enabled flag, and global/per-CSI pending quotas. Preflight variable/secret references without persisting values. Disabled execution returns `503 DISPATCH_DISABLED`; full admission returns 429.
2. In one transaction, snapshot the confirmed revision, CSI, environment, nonsecret configuration, principal and references; insert `PENDING` history plus its globally unique dispatch ledger row. Persist idempotency-key/request-digest mapping here, scoped to principal and route, so retry across API replicas returns the same execution. Existing in-memory idempotency middleware alone is insufficient. Return 202 only after commit.
3. The dedicated worker dispatcher claims queued ledger rows transactionally with a lease. Recheck current execution/secret authorization and resolve values immediately before dispatch. A vanished secret or revoked permission becomes a terminal `ERROR` with an explicit code. Values are ephemeral and sent over encrypted internal transport.
4. Persist an attempt ID and `DISPATCHING` state before the HTTP send. `POST /v1/runs` is a short admission request. The runner reserves capacity and performs an authenticated admission CAS through the API before launching Chromium. Only one `(runnerInstanceId, admissionId)` can own an attempt; duplicate identical admission is idempotent and competing admission gets 409. A failed admission handshake never starts a browser.
5. Runner responds 202 after admission, then starts execution. `RUNNING` is written only on an authenticated browser-start report, not when an HTTP call starts. An admitted-but-not-started run has a bounded start deadline.

Runner 429 means definite nonacceptance: no durable admission and no browser started. Retry it with `Retry-After`/jitter within the pending deadline. Timeouts, connection loss, or 5xx are ambiguous: consult admission/progress/manifest state and await recovery; do not resend browser work. Disable automatic POST retries in clients and proxies. Expired leases may reclaim work only when no dispatch attempt was issued; a dispatcher crash between recording an attempt and sending it may intentionally end as unknown rather than risk duplicate effects.

### 5.2 Runner lifecycle

For recorded observed replay: Validate request/artifact → acquire slot → admission handshake → launch Chromium → create one persistent context with native recording → perform fixed trusted preference/profile verification on its sole startup page → close that page and await/delete only its confined no-secret native video → create the sole clean application page at about:blank → establish its blank world and recording readiness → sample the existing paired run origin once → validate blank evidence and report browser start → execute permitted operations with step-start/finish reporting. For recorded observed replay, the same fixed persistent context may use one trusted startup page solely for chrome://version, chrome://prefs-internals and about:blank verification. At most one page is active at any instant. Before application navigation, source/blank-world evidence, browser secret delivery or action, run-origin sampling and Ready, close that page, await finalization and delete only its owned no-secret startup native video inside confined per-run scratch, then create the sole about:blank application page. Install phase-specific page guards from startup and the ordinary extra-application-page refusal before exposing the application page. Install the guard at first context acquisition with immediate reconciliation of the startup page set; authorize only the specifically issued application newPage operation after the startup page is closed and its artifact is deleted. Latch any unexpected-page event permanently for this launch, including events before the child subscribes; page replacement or late callback registration cannot clear or lose it. Refuse readiness on the latch even if the unexpected page was already closed. Unexpected pages, unsafe paths, failed or unbounded close/delete, missing effective preferences or confinement mismatch fail before Ready; no fallback or diagnostic video upload is permitted. On probe, video finalization/deletion, cancellation, deadline or context failure, refuse Ready and dispose the actual context/browser; late launch completion after stop is disposed too. The parent bounds or forces process-tree teardown and scratch/capacity release. Never swallow startup cleanup failure, choose a stray recording or wait indefinitely for native video. Parent/child start and absolute admission/run deadlines continue across every startup step and cleanup; neither page replacement nor clock sampling resets or extends them. Sample the existing paired wall/monotonic run origin once at clean application-page recording readiness, validate its blank world before Ready, and retain measured pinned-recorder seek calibration. Clean app-page readiness is established before the existing one-time paired origin sample and blank-world/liveness check before Ready. An application recording may have a measured bounded blank prefix; actual pinned native-recorder calibration must still meet the existing controlled-fixture seek target within 500 ms for initial navigation and failure. No diagnostic-prefix arithmetic or virtual timing result substitutes for decoded native video or outstanding staging calibration. Keep the existing admitted runtime budget/window and continuous absolute run/parent deadlines; do not grant a new runtime allowance on page replacement. Only this application page supplies native app video; no rewrite, merge, transcode, diagnostic-prefix subtraction or altered application recording is allowed. Native partial/evidence state remains determined by actual application recording finalization, independently of outcome. Guided unrecorded startup currently stays unchanged; OBS-013 must record the same sole clean application page in its existing guided context. This sequential trusted bootstrap exception does not permit popups, multi-page application workflows, extra contexts, browser modes, arguments, sandbox bypass, new wire fields or image-provenance waiver. Backend resolution may already precede launch; this rule makes no claim of zero backend Vault reads or releases during startup. Default step timeout is 30 seconds and total browser runtime 120 seconds, configurable within server limits. Stop on the first step failure; remaining steps become `SKIPPED` with null timings. Unexpected popups are closed and reported as unsupported rather than silently continuing on another page.

The runner refuses to launch after the server-issued admission/start deadline; the parent enforces total deadline and kills the child process tree on a hang. Close context to flush video when possible, upload evidence, publish the terminal manifest/result, then clean scratch files and release capacity on every path. Launch and close a browser per run. Initial `POOL_SIZE=1`; measure before increasing it.

### 5.3 Durable progress and results

- Internal reports carry execution/attempt/admission identities and increasing `runnerSequence`. Progress uses cumulative step/log state, bounded and redacted. API verifies ownership and sequence, applies changes conditionally, and increments its own `revision` for every visible state change, including reaper/evidence updates.
- Terminal reports use the same path. Before delivery, runner writes a redacted terminal result manifest to a deterministic Sonic key containing attempt/revision identity, result, timings, runtime versions, and evidence state. No resolved variables/secrets enter manifests.
- Retry terminal delivery until acknowledged within a bounded delivery window. The API acknowledges only after commit. If a process dies after manifest upload, recovery reads the known key and applies the result idempotently. No bucket listing or durable callback URL is required.
- If Sonic is unavailable, still deliver the final result directly with evidence failure. If both API delivery and durable storage fail before runner loss, no complete result can be guaranteed; the reaper records infrastructure failure.
- Conditional transitions prevent delayed progress/results from overwriting a finalized execution or another admission. Recovery checks the manifest before finalizing an ambiguous timeout. A manifest arriving after finalization is recorded for investigation; it cannot silently change history or trigger a new run.

### 5.4 Recovery and backpressure (V1)

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Queued without issued attempt, dispatcher lease expired | Reclaim within pending deadline |
| Pending deadline exceeded without admission | `ERROR / DISPATCH_FAILED`; use `DISPATCH_UNKNOWN` if send outcome is ambiguous |
| Admitted but browser start deadline exceeded | Reconcile matching report/manifest, otherwise `ERROR / START_TIMEOUT` |
| Running beyond fixed runtime + finalization/delivery margin | Reconcile manifest, otherwise `ERROR / STALE` |
| Outcome known but evidence/delivery not settled by deadline | Preserve check outcome, settle evidence as failed/unavailable and set `streamComplete` |

Both pending and running reapers plus finalization recovery ship in V1 on the worker profile. Derive deadlines from persisted timestamps; heartbeats never extend the maximum run deadline indefinitely. Bound dispatcher threads/connections, compile work, pending rows per CSI/globally, callback body size, and SSE subscriptions. Test overload while ordinary REST/check traffic continues.

Disabling `studio.execution.enabled` rejects new executes, closes queued undispatched work as `ERROR / DISPATCH_DISABLED`, and lets admitted work finish and report. Keep callbacks, recovery, reads and video serving available. Drain before removing a runner Deployment.

### 5.5 SSE progress

`GET /executions/{id}/events` returns `text/event-stream` using Spring MVC `SseEmitter`. Initial and reconnect delivery is a full current execution snapshot. Event type is `execution.snapshot`; `id` is the API snapshot revision. The MFE replaces current state, ignores older revisions, and never re-executes because a connection failed.

Each API replica batches DB reads for its locally watched execution IDs every 500–1000 ms and broadcasts only changed snapshots. Share a read across viewers of a run; no sticky sessions or broker are required. Intermediate transitions may coalesce, but final step status, timings, and bounded retained logs survive. `Last-Event-ID` supports reconnect identification; V1 promises current-state recovery, not lossless event replay. Include `logsTruncated` when the configured retained-log cap is reached.

Send heartbeat comments every 15 seconds. Use an explicit bounded stream lifetime (initially 60 seconds) and reconnect to refresh identity/CSI authorization. Set `Cache-Control: no-store`; disable buffering through the actual gateway/ingress; idle timeouts must exceed heartbeat cadence. Native EventSource uses the approved session-cookie route; a bearer-only platform requires a header-capable client inside the centralized API service. No credential query parameters. Verify cross-origin cookie/CORS behavior where applicable.

Use bounded dedicated senders and coalesced per-client pending snapshots; slow clients must not block callbacks, DB readers, or ordinary check workers. Clean up on error/timeout/completion and component unmount. One subscription per actively viewed execution. Close explicitly on `streamComplete=true`, after evidence is settled. On persistent transport failure use the authorized GET snapshot with bounded polling; distinguish 401/403 via the normal client and stop rather than falling back around denied access.

Validate streaming through the actual proxy/auth route before rollout; a demonstrated incompatibility uses GET fallback without changing the execution contract. [Spring MVC](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc/mvc-ann-async.html) supports this streaming model.

## 6. Video proof & playback

### 6.1 Recording and evidence state

For recorded observed replay: Record native webm on the sole application page in the single persistent context. The fixed trusted sequential startup page may produce a separate no-secret native video solely for preference/profile verification; close it and await/delete only that owned startup video before application-page creation and Ready. That startup artifact is never app evidence, a manifest/video key candidate or an uploaded recording; deletion never edits application video. Await finalization and deletion within the continuous start/absolute run/parent deadlines; unsafe ownership/path/symlink, video error, cancellation or failed deletion refuses Ready and requires bounded cleanup. The close result may return only the actual application page-owned recording after awaited app/context closure, never a directory-selected fallback. Existing native resolution, partial/evidence state, outcome independence, 30-day video expiry and authenticated key derivation remain. Other existing paths retain their current recording scope; OBS-013 adds clean guided recording separately. Await context closure to finalize the file; sudden process death may leave no playable recording. Explicitly configure video resolution so the text needed for evidence remains readable. [Playwright video documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/videos) describes context finalization and per-page recordings.

Keep outcome (`PASSED | FAILED | ERROR`) separate from evidence: `PROCESSING | AVAILABLE | FAILED | UNAVAILABLE | EXPIRED`. Upload failure never overwrites a known assertion outcome. `UNAVAILABLE` covers runs without a usable recording; `FAILED` covers evidence production/upload failures. Expose `videoError`, `videoExpiresAt`, and whether an available recording is partial. `streamComplete` means run processing/evidence delivery is settled, not that retention can no longer change availability.

### 6.2 Storage

Private keys:

- Video: `studio/{csiId}/{testId}/{executionId}/{attemptId}.webm`.
- Result manifest: `studio/{csiId}/{testId}/{executionId}/{attemptId}.result.json`.

The API derives expected keys from immutable execution identity; client-supplied keys are never trusted. Runner writes only this prefix; API/recovery read only. Runner has no Get/List permissions. Use encrypted transport/storage under platform policy. Manifests and videos expire after 30 days via lifecycle rules; verify versioning/noncurrent-object and incomplete-upload cleanup semantics on Sonic. Enforce logical video expiry in the API at `videoExpiresAt` even if physical lifecycle deletion is asynchronous. Track deletion compliance; do not claim exact-time physical deletion before Sonic behavior is verified.

### 6.3 Playback and download

`GET /executions/{id}/video` checks the execution's immutable CSI, including for soft-deleted tests, then streams from Sonic. Support ordinary 200, single byte Range/206, valid `Content-Range`, and invalid/unsatisfiable range 416. Return a clear expired/unavailable response when appropriate. `?download=true` uses the same authorization with an attachment filename derived by the API. Store object keys only; expose the protected API path to the browser.

An authenticated ambient session/gateway route is required for `<video>` and download requests; same-origin alone does not supply a JavaScript bearer header. This is a staging prerequisite shared with SSE. Presigned redirects are post-V1, contingent on desktop reachability and access policy.

### 6.4 Step seek

For each attempted step persist `offsetMs` (start on recording timeline) and `durationMs`. Use a monotonic runner clock and calibrate its origin against the pinned recorder's first frames. V1 acceptance target: seek within 500 ms of the visible step start on the controlled fixture, including initial navigation and failure cases; validate this target in staging before claiming it for real applications. Clicking a wait/assertion seeks its start, not necessarily the later instant its condition becomes true. `SKIPPED` steps have null timing and disabled seek. No synthetic index-times-ten mapping remains.

## 7. Scheduling and platform integration (post-V1)

Legacy `ui_tests.schedule`/status fields remain nonoperational. STUDIO-SCHED-001 implements the post-V1 scheduling extension through dedicated typed schedule/activation/occurrence records, server recurrence, and the existing Studio acceptance/readiness/authorization/quota/dispatch ledger. The producer defaults off and production grants remain release gated. See [ADR-003](ADR-003-studio-test-scheduling.md), the [approved specification](../stories/STUDIO-SCHED-001/spec/spec.md), and [operations](../specs/studio/scheduling/operations.md). Scheduled work never compiles implicitly; due readiness refusals explicitly record `COMPILE_REQUIRED`. Ambiguous UI attempts never enter generic automatic retry.

STUDIO-SCHED-002 consolidates recurring check/Studio production under shared `SchedulingCoordinator`/`SchedulingTargetWorker` and `CronRecurrence`, with existing `CronDispatcher` and `StudioScheduledTarget` adapters. See [ADR-004](ADR-004-shared-check-scheduling.md). Catalog executors and Studio acceptance/ledger/runner remain domain-owned; no public contract or storage change is implied.

V1 owns Studio history and last-run summaries by CSI. The association between `UI_TEST` checks and Studio definitions, application/component metadata, and unified dashboard/report projections must be specified in the later integration story; updating a Studio row alone does not populate those views. Preserve optional `checkId` in history for that integration. Scheduling and unified reporting controls must not imply that an unsupported path is operational in V1.

## 8. Data model & API contracts

### 8.1 Drafts and immutable revisions

Add forward-only migrations; retain legacy history without pretending it had confirmed artifacts.

| Entity | Required data |
|---|---|
| `ui_tests` | Non-null registered immutable `csi_id`; source/configuration revisions; compile request ID/status/diagnostics; current candidate and confirmed revision IDs; existing metadata/steps/variables/configuration |
| `ui_test_revisions` (new) | Immutable UUID; test/CSI; source/configuration revisions; ordered source/hash; artifact/hash/schema version; nonsecret configuration and declared references; model/prompt/reference/validator/executor/runtime compatibility provenance; creator/time and write-once confirmation identity/time |
| Execution history | Immutable revision reference and CSI; nonsecret execution snapshot/principal; actual runtime versions; timing, outcome, evidence and logs |
| Dispatch ledger (new, unpartitioned) | Globally unique `execution_id`; history partition locator; persistent execute-idempotency key/digest; attempt and admission identities; claim lease/state/deadlines; last runner sequence and API snapshot revision; deterministic manifest key |

`artifactHash` covers canonical artifact bytes; the immutable revision binds source and configuration. Ordinary test CRUD cannot alter revision history. Legacy executions retain their provenance limits rather than acquiring fabricated confirmation metadata.

### 8.2 Execution migrations and states

- Status constraint: `PENDING | RUNNING | PASSED | FAILED | ERROR`.
- Keep legacy `started_at` as an immutable acceptance/partition timestamp for existing monthly partition compatibility. Public `acceptedAt` maps to it. Add nullable `browser_started_at`; public `startedAt` maps to that. Never change the partition key when the browser begins.
- Make `ended_at` and `duration_ms` nullable in both SQL and Java types. `durationMs` measures browser execution when it started; queue duration is separate.
- Add immutable CSI/revision reference, `step_results` JSONB, structured bounded log storage, video key/state/error/expiry/partial flag, runtime provenance and snapshot metadata. Backfill legacy CSI only where ownership is known; quarantine ambiguous/null-CSI history from user access pending explicit migration resolution.
- The current table has `(id, started_at)` as its primary key. Ledger `execution_id` is globally unique and carries the partition locator; repositories must honor the physical composite key for update/recovery. Do not introduce an invalid single-column foreign key to the partitioned table.
- Add pending/running/deadline indexes on the ledger and verify migration behavior on historical, current, future and default history partitions.
- Widen `ui_tests.last_run_status` to include `ERROR`; update last-run projection only when the finishing execution is newer by `(acceptedAt, executionId)` than the projected one. An older late completion must not overwrite a newer run.

Per-step states: `PENDING | RUNNING | PASS | FAIL | SKIPPED`. Return one result entry per original step. Skipped/unstarted timings are null. `PENDING` is accepted but not yet browser-started; `RUNNING` means an authenticated runner-start report was committed. Timeouts are `ERROR` with a code, not a distinct execution status. A step locator/assertion timeout is `FAIL` and execution `FAILED`; a parent-enforced total timeout is `ERROR / TIMEOUT`.

### 8.3 Public API (base `/api/v1/studio`)

| Route | Contract |
|---|---|
| `GET /tests`, `GET /tests/{id}` | Typed test DTOs; lists filter all results by readable CSI, even without `csiId` |
| `POST /tests`, `PUT /tests/{id}` | Registered CSI required; immutable CSI; typed steps/configuration; optimistic revisions; persist draft only; preparing the saved revision is the Run action's explicit compile request |
| `DELETE /tests/{id}` | Soft delete; reject new execute/compile; retain authorized history |
| `POST /tests/{id}/compile` | 202 plus compile request identity; bounded async retry for current source |
| `POST /tests/{id}/confirm-compile` | Exact revision/hash/source/configuration body from §4.2; 409 on stale candidate |
| `POST /tests/{id}/execute` | Durable principal-scoped idempotency key; 202 `{executionId}`; 409 readiness/runtime conflict, 400 invalid references/configuration, 429 quota, 503 disabled |
| `GET /executions?testId=` | Paged history; `testId` optional; always filter by immutable execution CSI |
| `GET /executions/{id}` | Current snapshot including revision, step results/logs, evidence state and `streamComplete` |
| `GET /executions/{id}/events` | Authorized SSE snapshots; same data contract as GET |
| `GET /executions/{id}/video` | Protected video stream; optional `download=true` |

Freeze one OpenAPI/JSON-schema contract and MSW fixtures in story 10.1 before wiring frontend/backend. Use `steps: string[]`, typed `variables` (`plain` or `secretRef`), `configuration: {browser, viewport, timeoutSeconds, waitStrategy}`, and `environment` in test requests. The server generates structured artifacts; clients never submit executable code as authoritative.

Canonical browser value is `chromium`. A migration adapter accepts legacy `chrome` and normalizes it; other engines reject before execution. Migrate the DB browser constraint/current rows explicitly. Convert legacy structured `TestIR` to ordered `originalText`, JSON strings to typed DTO fields, flattened viewport fields to `configuration.viewport`, and legacy `COMPLETED/TIMEOUT` to the canonical outcome contract. Remove client grammar validation and Python generation as authoritative paths. Include schedule/status editing only when that capability ships.

### 8.4 Internal HTTP contracts

All internal routes require restricted service identity and encrypted transport; they are not exposed through public ingress.

| Route | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Runner `POST /v1/validate` | Browser-free schema/AST/policy validation plus per-step diagnostics |
| Runner `POST /v1/runs` | Short admission: 202 admitted; 400 invalid, 401/403 unauthorized, 409 competing/expired admission, 429 definite nonacceptance. A 5xx or transport loss is ambiguous |
| API `POST /internal/studio/executions/{id}/admission` | CAS exclusive ownership by attempt + runner instance + admission identity; duplicate same identity acknowledged; no browser starts without success |
| API `POST /internal/studio/executions/{id}/progress` | Cumulative STARTED/PROGRESS/FINAL snapshots; validate ownership, sequence, transitions, redaction and limits; acknowledge after commit |

# Secret-reference login in guided runs — technical design

Status: **R3 — canonical design for secret-reference login on the single observed path ([ADR-SC-005](../../architecture/ADR-SC-005-single-path-observed-authoring.md)).** Written by Aria (@architect), 2026-10-09; R3 the same day after the user accepted the single-path ruling. Design only: no code, schema, migration, OpenAPI, test or story file is changed by this document. Every `path:line` below was read on this working tree on 2026-10-09 (HEAD `d954a21c5`); line numbers drift. R3 removes every legacy-compile-path variant (the compile path is retired by STUDIO-OBS-012A): the password-only rule has one adapter and no opt-out; `LOGIN_REQUIRED` is computed from the observation signature on both guided learn and observed replay; migrations follow the ADR-SC-005 D-B re-baseline (V34 absorbed); the backend→runner hop is one TLS/client-certificate hop to one runner process; §10 maps items onto the ADR-SC-005 story set. ## 2. Target flow (one page)

```
author: "Enter <var USER> as username" / "Enter <secret PASS> as password" / "Click Sign in" / "Open reports" / …
  classify  → sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:PASS}; preflight(mayUse + exists), no read
  plan      → model sees step text with the token span masked, the reference (ID), never a value
  materialize → authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId:PASS}  (no value; hashed into authoredInputsHash)
  propose   → fill.value = {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}, target = {kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}  (node-free: the collector never exports a password node)
  prepare   → mayUse recheck (names only); trusted runner proves exactly one visible enabled input[type=password] in the current top-level document
  dispatch  → backend resolve() from Vault (CSI/env/testId/principal scope), RELEASE audit row, send BridgeDispatch.secret on mTLS bridge, erase
  act       → trusted runner re-resolves that unique password input at fill time (0 or >1 ⇒ POLICY_DENIED), origin ∈ allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins, withhold(value) BEFORE fill, fill via the pinned handle
  observe   → next observation is the reached document; knownSecrets scrubs any echo
  publish   → artifact fill value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}; inputRecipes {kind:secretRef, referenceName:PASS}; no value anywhere
  replay    → job.secrets/secretOrigins resolved per run by the ordinary dispatch pass, same origin + password rule in the observed adapter, model-free
  stop      → knownSecrets = [], inventory disposed, dispatch frame not retained
```
